original_question: Describe the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration. In particular, for a specific Costas permutation or a specific family, determine the full cycle decomposition, whether cycles of a given length can occur, the longest cycle length, and the smallest positive integer k for which the k-fold iterate equals the identity permutation.
target_in_paper: Problem 9 in Section 4.4 ("Cycle structure of Costas permutations").
correct_elements: Your draft already captures Problem 9 almost verbatim: it asks for the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration and includes all four paper-stated subquestions—full cycle decomposition for a particular Costas permutation, existence/absence of cycles of a given length, longest cycle length, and the least positive iterate returning the identity, either for a single permutation or for a family.
missing_details: State the ambient finite set explicitly: [n] = {1, ..., n}.
Define a Costas permutation explicitly as a bijection f:[n] -> [n] whose distance vectors {(i-j, f(i)-f(j)) : 1 <= j < i <= n} are all distinct.
Define the iterate notation used in the paper: f^(0) = I and f^(k+1) = f o f^(k), where I(i) = i is the identity permutation on [n].
Define the cycle of i under f as {f^(k)(i) : k in N}; then 'cycle structure' means the resulting disjoint cycle decomposition of f.

Clarify that the final quantity is the least positive k such that f^(k) = I, since Definition 9 already has f^(0) = I; equivalently, this is determined by the least common multiple of the cycle lengths.
State explicitly that this is a purely finite-permutation/combinatorial question; there are no ambient field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses in this problem.
refined_question: Let [n] = {1, ..., n}, and let f:[n] -> [n] be a Costas permutation, meaning that f is a bijection such that the distance vectors {(i-j, f(i)-f(j)) : 1 <= j < i <= n} are all distinct. Write f^(0) = I for the identity permutation on [n], and define f^(k+1) = f o f^(k) for k >= 0. For i in [n], let the cycle of i under f be the finite set {f^(k)(i) : k in N}. For a given Costas permutation f, or for a specified family of Costas permutations, determine the disjoint cycle decomposition of f; decide which cycle lengths occur and which are absent; determine the maximum cycle length; and determine the least positive integer k such that f^(k) = I.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent only for the last subquestion: after determining the disjoint cycle decomposition of f, determine the least common multiple of its cycle lengths, since f^(k) = I exactly when k is a multiple of that least common multiple.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Problem 9 in Section 4.4, not a broader neighboring problem. Its wording reproduces the four bullets of Problem 9 almost exactly. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the only additions needed are the paper's notation [n] = {1, ..., n}, the Definition 1 meaning of 'Costas permutation', and the Definition 9 meanings of iteration, identity, and cycle. One clarification is necessary: because Definition 9 already sets f^(0) = I, the intended last item must be the least positive k with f^(k) = I; the sentence immediately following the example in Section 4.4 explains that this is controlled by the least common multiple of the cycle lengths.
